title: The warmer school year
hook: Does a temperature-learning association look the same with cooling available?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish environmental exposure from its moderation by air conditioning.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish environmental exposure from its moderation by air conditioning.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In a toy exposure rule, one extra degree causes a 1% learning loss with no attenuation. What is the modeled change? Toy inputs A=[1, 1, 0]; B=[1, 1, 0.8].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[-1, 1, 0], [-0.19999999999999996, 1, 80]]. Labels: Learning change %, Extra °F, Attenuation %.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The second case moderates the temperature effect while keeping exposure fixed. An exposure coefficient and a protective moderator are different inputs. The toy is not an independently verified estimate for a particular school or climate.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Extra °F=1, Loss per °F=1, AC attenuation=0.8. What is Learning change %? Answer: -0.2.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Extra °F=1, Loss per °F=1, AC attenuation=0.8. What is Learning change %?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives -0.2. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: A school year 1°F hotter, without air conditioning, reduced learning about 1% (Park, Goodman, Hurwitz & Smith, 2020).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish environmental exposure from its moderation by air conditioning.
